# SEO-288: Publish corrections in the page body rather than only a changelog

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

## Statement

When a published claim turns out to be wrong, the correction appears in the passage that carried the claim, not solely in a revision note elsewhere on the page or in a separate log.

## Rationale

A system that retrieved the passage holds the passage, so a correction recorded only in a footer or a separate log leaves the wrong sentence intact in every copy that was taken.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "content_publication",
    "editorial_content"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Amend the sentence itself and mark the amendment inline, keeping the revision note as a record of what changed rather than as the only place the correction exists.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: For each recorded correction, confirm the amended text is present in the passage it belongs to and not only in a revision note.
- Evidence: `RENDERED_HTML`, `MANUAL_ACTION`, `ROUTE`
- Automated check: none.

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `AI_ASSISTANT_RETRIEVAL`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: This record rests on the fact that a retrieved copy is a copy, which needs no citation. How long any particular system holds a copy, or whether it refetches, is not documented by its operator and is not claimed here.
